title: Light-Emitting Diode Floor Proximity Marking in the Passenger Cabin

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: A low-current light-emitting diode floor marking replaces both the incandescent powered strip and the photoluminescent option, removing the charge time restriction while keeping most of the weight and power benefit.

sections.reason: The photoluminescent option removed the electrical load but introduced a charge time restriction that operators found unworkable on dark overnight turnarounds, and two operators reverted at their own cost. A low-current light-emitting diode strip had by then become available with a certified twelve-minute autonomy from a distributed battery, giving the weight and load benefit without the operational restriction. The change was launched to give a single forward standard and to close out the reversion requests.
sections.description: A continuous light-emitting diode strip is installed along the seat track cover line on both aisles and around each exit, powered from distributed battery units at four cabin stations. The exit marker assembly D3320137300785 carries the local battery and the driver, and tubular spacers AES27771-7A are retained from the earlier standard to set the panel standoff. The exit panel 841LP7 and the inboard stowage marker 850LP6 both receive new lenses. Arrangement is on drawing D33200083632. Work is in zones 291 and 951 with carpet lifted along the aisle and the exit surrounds opened. The powered floor marking wiring, where still present, is removed and capped at the seat track junction.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 17 kg per aircraft compared with the original powered installation, and an increase of 5 kg compared with the photoluminescent option. Emergency electrical load reduced by 260 VA. Not interchangeable with either earlier standard. The charge time placard and the associated cabin crew procedure are removed. The floor marking functional test returns but at a twelve-month rather than a six-month interval, and the illustrated parts content requires a pre and post item pair at every marker position.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00407 in December 2023. Retrofit through Service Bulletin MRD-33-1064, which is written for aircraft already at the photoluminescent standard and takes three shifts with four people during a cabin visit.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, no reportable CG shift
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN M00407, cabin lighting supplier standard change
